source_review.notes: Checked current RFC 9110 method, status, Location, validator, and precondition semantics; RFC 9111 unsafe-method cache invalidation; and RFC 6585 status 428. Domain lifecycle claims are labeled as application policy rather than protocol guarantees.

notation_and_syntax.notes: State, stimulus, transition, and validator notation is introduced before use and rendered with supported math delimiters.

numerical_recomputation.notes: No derived numerical claim is made.

evidence: GET safety separated from incidental effects
PUT repeat preserves intended desired state
DELETE changes URI association without implying physical erasure
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Method and transition consequences were re-derived from stated protocol premises; implementation and domain effects remain bounded.

boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary review covers concurrency, retries, durability, caches, privacy, lifecycle, and partial observation.

invariant_checking.notes: All five invariants hold across examples, exercises, and recovery guidance.

proof_review.notes: No formal correctness proof is claimed.

evidence: cache invalidation is not global coherence
timeout is not proof of failure
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter makes no empirical production claim and appropriately omits artificial code.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed CRUD versus HTTP semantics, GET/HEAD safety, POST processing, PUT creation/replacement, DELETE lifecycle, status codes, preconditions, caching, and outcome ambiguity.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed authorization, request validation, duplicate effects, conditional concurrency, durable acceptance, archival and erasure, cache invalidation, derived views, retries, and operation lookup.

pedagogical_review.notes: Ten examples cover distinct method and lifecycle failures; five exercises progress from mapping critique through concurrency, diagnosis, design comparison, and spacecraft transfer, with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
